incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become a target of artificial intelligence scammers who are stealing his identity to defraud vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos featuring Leal offering immigration services he never provides, such as promising US residency for $2,200. The scams escalated dramatically in recent months, with fraudsters using WhatsApp to direct victims to send money through payment apps like Venmo and Zelle while exchanging fake contracts.

Leal discovered the scheme when potential clients began calling his office about services advertised on social media. His firm hired an anti-piracy company that has successfully removed nearly 6,500 fake accounts, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities to investigate the scams. He is warning immigrants to verify the identity of anyone offering legal services online and to be suspicious of social media advertisements requesting immediate payments.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fake article circulating online falsely depicted Reserve Bank Governor Michele Bullock in a heated interview with ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler about Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform. The interview never actually occurred. This fabricated content represents a growing category of scam that uses artificial intelligence to create convincing deepfakes and fake news articles featuring well-known Australians. The corporate regulator ASIC reports these AI-generated investment schemes are becoming increasingly sophisticated and harder to detect.

ASIC's latest research reveals a significant rise in investment scams, with the regulator removing 19,400 schemes last year, a 182 percent increase. The agency took down 7,051 fake investment platforms and 5,476 phishing scams. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and finance presenter Alan Kohler rank among the most commonly impersonated Australians, alongside politicians like Pauline Hanson and business figures including Dick Smith and Gina Rinehart. ASIC warns consumers to verify financial service licenses and avoid investing based on celebrity endorsements or online testimonials, as scammers build elaborate webs of fake websites, reviews, and advertisements to deceive potential investors.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A class-action lawsuit filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco accuses Oura, a smart ring company valued at 11 billion dollars, of false advertising regarding its sleep tracking capabilities. The suit claims that Oura rings, which cost 300 dollars and up, cannot accurately measure sleep stages as advertised. The lawsuit alleges that the company's algorithms and sensors lack the ability to detect the physiological signals needed for accurate sleep stage measurement and instead rely on artificial intelligence guesses that are no better than random chance.

Oura disputes the allegations, stating that its rings track sleep stages using multiple physiological signals including heart rate and breathing patterns. The company claims its sleep staging has been validated in peer-reviewed studies and compared favorably against clinical sleep lab standards. However, CNET experts note that wearable health trackers like the Oura Ring provide estimates rather than medical-grade measurements and should not be overemphasized. The lawsuit seeks class action status and a jury trial, though it remains unclear what compensation buyers might receive if the case proceeds or settles. This lawsuit follows a previous class action against Oura alleging unauthorized collection of personal data.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group has been active since April 2026 and developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi environments. The group operated a data leak site and attacked organizations across multiple countries. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent running Claude Sonnet to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten target organizations. The ESXi ransomware variant encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. Attackers used a custom tool called esxi_finder.py to scan networks for ESXi hosts and vCenter servers.

In separate activity, Gambit identified a second Aurora cluster affecting eight organizations across Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. This second group used different methods including exposed SQL Server commands, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration to cloud storage. The attackers imposed strict operational rules when using AI tools, repeatedly forbidding DCSync attacks, account lockouts, and adding new domain computers. Gambit provided indicators of compromise including IP addresses, URLs, and file hashes to help organizations identify and defend against these threats.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the northeastern United States, filed a lawsuit in Texas Business Court on May 6 alleging that Pizza Hut's mandatory adoption of Dragontail, an AI-powered delivery management system, caused over $100 million in damages. The franchisee claims the system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, causing drivers to wait up to fifteen minutes to batch multiple orders together rather than delivering completed pizzas immediately, which significantly delayed deliveries and reduced customer satisfaction.

Before Dragontail's 2024 rollout, Chaac maintained over 90 percent on-time delivery rates and double-digit sales growth, but performance sharply deteriorated afterward. In New York City alone, year-over-year sales growth dropped from positive 10.19 percent to negative 9.78 percent. The lawsuit accuses Pizza Hut of breaching its franchise agreement by mandating continued use of the problematic software while refusing adequate support and ignoring worsening metrics. Pizza Hut stated it is reviewing the claims and will respond through legal channels but declined further comment.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other staff members of NPR's Fresh Air program to defraud people. The fraudulent emails target authors, entertainers and public figures with highly personalized interview invitations that appear legitimate, including detailed references to their work and professional booking processes. Recipients are eventually asked to pay fees for production costs, though some are also directed to provide social media login credentials. WHYY, NPR and Fresh Air have confirmed they are aware of these fraudulent emails and are working with law enforcement to investigate.

Cybersecurity experts attribute the increasing sophistication of these scams to artificial intelligence, which allows criminals to personalize impersonation attempts cheaply and convincingly. Red flags include requests for payment, emails from unofficial addresses like terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com, and the unusual situation of a major show's host personally handling logistics. WHYY clarified that it never charges guests for interviews. Experts recommend verifying suspicious requests by contacting the organization directly through legitimate channels rather than responding to the suspicious message.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded organization called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy, which does not appear to exist as a legal entity, created a fake think tank website designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots. Between August 6 and 14, the site published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words framed as neutral research, covering topics including Israeli military actions, Palestinian casualties, and genocide allegations. The reports were structured as questions users might ask chatbots and used academic formatting with citations to legitimate sources, but consistently presented information in ways that defended Israel and suggested claims could not be verified without court rulings. The operation was part of a larger Israeli government campaign financed through European advertising firm Havas Media and routed through multiple American contractors.

The broader effort involves tens of millions of dollars in spending, including $15 million to a company run by former Trump campaign manager Brad Parscale. Israeli officials have expressed frustration that despite substantial spending, American public opinion has turned sharply against Israel, with polling showing record opposition particularly among younger Americans. Researchers noted that while the campaign may successfully influence chatbot responses, it has failed to shift actual public opinion, suggesting the government views a political problem as purely a marketing challenge.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, and Warner Music have filed separate lawsuits against AI music generators Udio and Suno, alleging the companies scraped thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their systems. The labels claim the AI services not only illegally used massive amounts of music but also directly reproduce sections of famous songs by artists like The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Chuck Berry, and Mariah Carey. The companies have refused to disclose their training data and previously argued their use constitutes fair use.

To support their claims, the record labels demonstrated they could repeatedly recreate famous copyrighted songs by using targeted prompts that specified details like decade, genre, and artist style. For example, specific prompts generated outputs closely mimicking Green Day's American Idiot and Mariah Carey's holiday hit, even reproducing distinctive vocal characteristics and melodic elements. The labels submitted thousands of examples and a thumb drive of AI-generated music as evidence. The lawsuits also target unnamed individuals who allegedly helped the companies scrape music, setting up a significant legal battle over how generative AI can train on copyrighted material.

incidents.title: Sony Music moves to add more than 30,000 copyrighted recordings to its lawsuit against Udio
incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, which had been accused of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system. The dispute centered on Udio's ability to generate original music from text prompts, allegedly by learning from existing hits without permission. Under the settlement, Udio has agreed to launch a new platform next year that will only use authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share songs while compensating artists involved.

The agreement marks Udio's first licensing deal with a major music label and reflects ongoing tensions between the entertainment industry and AI companies. UMG, along with Sony Music and Warner Music Group, had originally sued Udio for creating songs with similar melodies and chords to popular tracks like The Temptations' "My Girl." Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by investors including will.i.am, has already accumulated millions of users since launching. The settlement's financial terms were not disclosed by either party.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

State Farm's defense lawyers apologized for submitting legal filings containing artificial intelligence-generated fake cases, nonexistent quotes, and false legal holdings in a Los Angeles lawsuit. The case involves homeowner Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, who sued State Farm and others after a 2020 fire destroyed her Carson home. While repairs were underway, a storm caused water damage, and after delays in getting State Farm's approval for additional repairs, the work was never completed. Meni-Siliga and her husband exhausted their savings, retirement accounts, declared bankruptcy, and lost their home to foreclosure.

Lawyer Jacquelene Robinson admitted using an AI tool called Irys to prepare motions, mistakenly believing it was connected to her law firm's legal research subscription and performed accuracy checks. She confirmed seven case citations across eight filings did not exist, along with incorrect case titles and fabricated quotes. The case is scheduled for trial in October. State Farm stated it expects its external lawyers to maintain the highest ethical standards and ensure the accuracy of all legal filings. The broader legal industry increasingly uses generative AI, with a worldwide database currently tracking 1,922 documented legal hallucinations.

stories.Headline: Pakistan and Saudi Arabia Extend Partnership in AI and Data
stories.Summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have agreed to deepen their cooperation in artificial intelligence, data governance, and emerging technologies. The agreement was announced following a meeting between Pakistan's Federal Minister for Information Technology and Telecommunication Shaza Fatima Khawaja and Saudi Data and Artificial Intelligence Authority President Abdullah bin Sharaf Alghamdi at the LEAP 2026 conference in Riyadh. The two nations plan to establish a comprehensive and long-term technology partnership.

During the discussion, Pakistan's minister outlined the country's national AI and data governance initiatives while reaffirming Pakistan's commitment to building a strong data ecosystem and growing its digital economy. Both countries intend to collaborate on emerging technologies and create a lasting framework for cooperation. The partnership reflects a broader regional focus on advancing artificial intelligence, digital infrastructure, technology skills, and data-driven development.

stories.Headline: Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic Bring Free AI Bootcamp to Denver Teens
stories.Summary:
The Mark Cuban Foundation and Tonic are offering a free artificial intelligence bootcamp to high school students in Denver this fall. The program is open to ninth through twelfth graders and will run over three consecutive Saturdays on October 31, November 7, and November 14. All costs including meals, transportation, and technology will be covered for participants at no charge. Applications close on September 30.

The bootcamp provides hands-on experience with AI tools and explores real-world applications across fields like healthcare, business, sports science, and career preparation. Students will work on a capstone project guided by industry mentors. This Denver bootcamp is one of more than 35 similar programs being hosted across the United States by various companies. Mark Cuban emphasized the importance of providing AI education to underserved students to prepare them for future educational and employment opportunities.

stories.Headline: Datametrex Plans to Focus on AI, Data Centre, and Patent Licensing
stories.Summary:
Datametrex AI Limited announced plans to shut down its healthcare operations to focus on artificial intelligence, data centre technology, and patent licensing. The company operates medical clinics in Edmonton, Calgary, and Vancouver, British Columbia, providing primary and emergency care services. The gradual wind-down aims to streamline the corporate structure, reduce operating costs and regulatory requirements, and improve financial performance by redirecting resources toward core business areas.

The company will manage the transition carefully, considering operational, financial, contractual, and regulatory factors. Management plans to assess opportunities to maximize value from healthcare assets during the process. The strategic shift allows Datametrex to concentrate capital and resources on artificial intelligence and data centre initiatives, which align with long-term objectives. The company indicated it would provide further updates as developments occur.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Headline: Ghana: Ai Will Enhance, Not Replace Surveyors - Ghis President
stories.Summary:
Emmanuel K. Cobbold, president of the Ghana Institution of Surveyors, addressed members at the organization's 57th Founder's Day Anniversary Celebration in Accra. He encouraged surveyors to adopt artificial intelligence and emerging technologies rather than viewing them as threats to their profession. Cobbold emphasized that while AI can assist with measurements, data analysis, and interpretation, professional surveying still requires human judgment, local expertise, and ethical responsibility. He warned that surveyors who fail to adapt to technological changes risk becoming obsolete as the profession evolves.

The institution is working to help members upgrade their skills to meet changing technological demands while maintaining professional integrity standards. Sarah Esi Ziddah, the organization's chief executive officer, noted that surveyors have significantly contributed to Ghana's development, including providing geospatial data during a boundary dispute with Côte d'Ivoire and supporting construction of an infectious disease center. The event brought together current and former members to recognize contributions to the profession and strengthen professional connections among the organization's widely dispersed membership.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

stories.Headline: Brazil's electoral court sets new standards for AI deepfakes after case involving Sen. Bolsonaro
stories.Summary:
Brazil's electoral court established new standards for identifying artificial intelligence-generated deepfakes in political advertising as the country prepares for October elections. The ruling came from a case involving opposition candidate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, who displayed AI-generated images of his imprisoned father, former President Jair Bolsonaro, at his party's convention in July. The court voted 4-3 to not punish Bolsonaro, determining the deepfake was used at a private event before his official candidacy announcement rather than as a public political advertisement.

In a separate 5-2 vote, the court defined political deepfakes as synthetic content created through artificial intelligence that realistically reproduces the image, voice, or speech of any person. These new standards will govern the vast amount of online campaign content from candidates leading up to the first round of voting on October 4. Broadcasters must allocate significant airtime for candidate advertisements, including 14 minutes daily for nearly 1,000 thirty-second ads.
